messages.content:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: The rent deposit is held without interest, since it will be applied to the rent for the last month of the tenancy.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
**Not enforceable.**

Under the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, a landlord may take a rent deposit and must apply it to the last rent period of the tenancy (s. 106(10)). That part of the clause is fine. But using the deposit for last month's rent does not remove the landlord's duty to pay interest on it.

Section 106(6) requires the landlord to pay the tenant interest on the rent deposit **every year**, at the rent increase guideline rate in effect when the payment is due. Instead of paying the interest out, the landlord may use it to top up the deposit so it matches the current rent (s. 106(7)). If the landlord does neither, the tenant may deduct the unpaid interest from a future rent payment (s. 106(9)).

A lease term saying the deposit is "held without interest" conflicts with s. 106. Section 4 of the Act makes any provision in a tenancy agreement that is inconsistent with the Act void, and s. 3(1) makes the Act apply even if the parties agreed otherwise. The tenant therefore keeps the right to annual interest regardless of what the lease says.

Verdict: not enforceable
Section: 106
